---
title: "Other agents"
---

The exercises are written for OpenCode, but the same questions transfer to other harnesses. This page was checked 2026-09-12. Use the current vendor documentation for installation and account requirements; do not assume flags or configuration paths match.

## Optional comparisons

**Antigravity.** Check its verified project-rules mechanism and sandbox/telemetry settings in the [official documentation](https://antigravity.google/). A telemetry toggle is not a confidentiality guarantee.

The retained [Antigravity setup recording](../media/videos/agy-setup.mp4) is a donor aid, not a promise that current screens or account flows are unchanged.

**Codex.** Consult the [Codex setup and sandboxing guides](https://developers.openai.com/codex/). Personal-account behaviour follows the account's current data controls; review the official opt-out/data-control page before using any non-toy material.

**Claude Code.** Use [Claude's installation and memory documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory). Claude discovers `CLAUDE.md` according to its own precedence rules and does not thereby gain a stronger OS boundary.

If an optional agent is installed in the image, launch it from the selected lab directory: `agy` (Antigravity), `codex` (Codex), or `claude` (Claude Code). Authenticate only through its documented browser/command flow. For comparison-only flags, verify current help first: Antigravity's `--dangerously-skip-permissions` approves all tool calls and is distinct from its `--sandbox`; Codex's `--ask-for-approval never` is distinct from `--sandbox danger-full-access`; Claude's `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is a permission mode, not a sandbox. Do not use these bypass modes on a host or with real data.

In every product, verify the actual working directory, instructions loaded, permissions, and files changed. If an alternative cannot run in the Codespace, observe its documentation or UI only and continue the lab with OpenCode.
